description: Authoritative registry of headless conformance suites across all RFC domains. This is the single owner of which suites exist, what they cover, how they build, and their expected outcome. Domains add ONE row here when they land a new conformance suite; the shared runner (tools/quality/conformance.py) builds, runs, and evidences every row uniformly so a suite can never silently drift out of the gate. Profiles own toolchain/flag facts (quality/profiles/); this manifest references them by id.

suites.description: Initial RFC 0019 lab slice: moving layered inputs, FSR 4.1.1 INT8 through the core graph, finite output, metadata rejection/reset, isolated views, exact fresh/reset comparison, failed recording recovery, zero Vulkan validation messages. Not complete scene, portal, skinned/translucent motion or product acceptance. Timing is advisory.
Seeded retained context on reset must fail the exact fresh/reset image comparison.

Hammer map-building loop (RFC/0002-progress.md, R08-LOOP): hammer_cli runs quality/workloads/hammer-loop-v1 command scripts through the shared command layer, tools/quality/vmf_map_build.py compiles each saved VMF (vbsp, fast vvis, LDR and HDR vrad) and boots it headless on native Vulkan (portal_boot.py: map active, player spawned, scene captured). room must save, compile sealed and boot; leak (north wall missing) must stop at the leak gate; dark (no light) must boot with a capture the lit room is at least 1.3x brighter than. Reports the author-to-playable time; about 30 s.

UI-driven Hammer conformance (RFC/0002-progress.md, R08-UI-TEST): builds hammer_gtk from source and drives it in a private headless mutter session the way a user makes a map. Widgets are found by accessible name over AT-SPI; pointer and keys enter through the compositor's RemoteDesktop input; view positions come from the status-bar coordinates. Grid [ [, Block tool, drag a 384x384 block in the top view and its 128-unit height in the front view, Return, F (hollow), Entity tool, click a player start and (dropdown: light) a light into the front view, F9 (save and compile). The oracle judges the saved VMF (six world solids, one player start and one light inside the room), the build record (compiled, not leaked) and the frames the live editor's render-core viewports showed (the top view draws the room's walls, the camera view shaded geometry). Controls: no-hollow (walls must fail) and no-light (light must fail) drive the same UI with one step left out. About 45 s. The viewport case (R17) opens the sample room with a generated VPK of two VTF textures mounted and judges the live viewports: the camera frame is textured; each frame is its view's logical size times the window's scale; F12 writes captures equal to the frame shown; three reloads of the mounted assets (Ctrl+Shift+R) with frames in flight and a dragged view divider each bring the views back textured at the new size; Ctrl+Q exits cleanly with no device resource left by the viewports. The properties case (Object Properties window) opens two lights made by the command layer with a generated FGD (--fgd), selects both (Ctrl+A), opens the window (Alt+Enter), checks the differing _distance shows as '(different values)' and the differing flag as an inconsistent check box, types a new _distance and presses Enter (apply), toggles the flag, then saves, undoes, saves, undoes and saves; the oracle requires both lights edited, one undo taking back only the flag on both and a second the value on both. Its control, properties-cancel, presses Cancel instead (distance must fail). The visgroups case (Visgroups panel, RFC 0018 F6) opens a red and a green block made by the command layer, the green one in the file's visgroup Other, with the viewport VPK mounted; it clicks the red block in the top view, presses New Visgroup, hides the new visgroup with its check box, shows it again and undoes three times, saving after each stage; the oracle requires the red block's pixels gone from the camera and top frames while hidden (the green block's kept) and back when shown, the hidden map to list the visgroup with the red solid in it and visgroupshown 0 (kept through a command-layer open and save), and three undos to leave only Other in the map and the panel. Its control, visgroups-other, hides Other instead (hidden.camera must fail). This row runs GTK as an X11 client (Xwayland); the .wayland row as a Wayland client, and the .scaled rows the viewport case at 2x on X11 and at a fractional monitor scale on Wayland. The replace-textures case (R08-REPLACE-TEXTURES) opens two textured blocks with the generated VPK mounted, opens Replace Textures from the Texture Application window's Replace... (the catalog action behind Tools > Replace Textures...), checks Find defaults to the current material and the selection scope is off with nothing selected, types the replacement, reads the live preview (6 faces in 1 solid), OK; the message is the legacy "6 textures replaced.", the camera frame loses the green material, and the saved maps after OK, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y hold both blocks replaced, the original, and both replaced again, also after the command layer reopens and saves the map. Its control, replace-textures-cancel, presses Cancel (replaced must fail).

corpus.hammer.ui with GTK as a Wayland client of the private compositor (every case but the properties pair, which places the pointer in the properties window from its X11 origin). A Wayland toplevel reports no ACTIVE state over AT-SPI here, so each key is judged by its effect. The replace-textures pair runs here too.
The viewport case of corpus.hammer.ui on X11 at GDK_SCALE=2: frames are twice the views' logical size, and captures, reloads, a resize and teardown hold at that scale.

The viewport case of corpus.hammer.ui on Wayland at a fractional monitor scale (the supported scale nearest 1.5, set through the private session's keyfile settings): frames are the views' logical size times that scale.

Edit-to-pixels budgets for the Hammer editor's viewports on the RFC 0016 render core (quality/budgets/hammer-viewport-v1.json): builds hammer_gtk and runs hammer_gtk --viewport-budget per row. Each sample moves one solid through the command layer and times until all four views' new frames are back on the host sequence from the render sequence. p95 and max are judged against the row's limits; a control judges the same samples against a 0.001 ms limit, which must be rejected. Needs a Vulkan device; opens no window.

The textured edit-to-pixels budget row (quality/budgets/hammer-viewport-v1.json, desktop-trust-fling-4-views-textured): as corpus.hammer.viewport-budget, with the camera view drawing every face batch through the unlit family with its base texture from the VPKs HAMMER_TEXTURE_VPKS names (Portal 2's portal2/pak01_dir.vpk; not in the repository, so the row is optional). Missing content fails the row's content check.

The engine CThreadPool as a platform.task-runner.v1 runner (RFC 0001 rank 11 'adapt existing queues'; RFC/0003-progress.md, R10-POOLRUNNER): the shared runner suite, including never-inline and shutdown under load, against the vstdlib pool runner and a SequencedTaskRunner over it on a real 4-thread pool; threadless and null pools and a missing timer are refused. Runs the Waf-built test from the --tests tree.

Job graphs on the real engine CThreadPool through vstdlib/jobgraph_pool_bridge (RFC/0003-progress.md): pooled particle frames equal the serial reference, graph states equal the deterministic executor, failures cancel dependents, and caller jobs overlap compute jobs; and the process compute pool as the borrowed backend roots lend providers (CreateComputePoolWorkerBackend, the render core's culling since 2026-09-28): it follows the pool the engine starts and stops, leaves it running when destroyed, runs a call made on one of the pool's own workers inline and counts it (RFC 0003's forbidden nested wait), and keeps a call from another pool's worker (the MatQueue pool's place) pooled and uncounted. Runs the Waf-built test from the --tests tree.

The GTK shell's GlibTaskRunner (RFC/0002-progress.md, R08-ASYNC-BUILD) through the shared platform.task-runner.v1 suite on a private GLib main context the test thread iterates (a runner whose thread is the driver's), plus a post from another thread that runs on the context's thread. Compiled by hammer/gtk/tests/glib_task_runner.sh with pkg-config glib-2.0; no display.

Hammer MCP end to end (RFC/0002-progress.md, R08-MCP): starts hammer_cli --mcp and speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC to it, parsing every reply with Python's json module. The tool list must match the command catalog. Through tool calls it authors the UI suite's room (block, hollow, player start, light) and builds it with build_map; hammer_ui_test.py's oracle judges the saved VMF and the leak-free build record. Controls on the same stream: a malformed line (-32700, null id), an unknown tool (-32602) and a failing command (isError) must leave info unchanged; stdout must hold only replies.

Native POSIX loader provider against a real fixture shared library built by the runner: the shared loader, isolation and scoped-ownership oracles, plus the fixture function's real result, a non-library file (provider error) and a bare name that must not be searched for.
Destroying the POSIX loader while it owns a library must abort.

platform.task-runner.v1 (RFC 0001 rank 11, RFC 0003 sequences; R10-RUNNERS): one shared suite (exactly once, never inline, delayed not early, sequence order, no overlap and publication, current sequence and thread, shutdown drops and refuses) against ManualTaskRunner on virtual time, ThreadTaskRunner, SequencedTaskRunner over a thread, a 4-thread test pool and a manual runner, and the test pool itself; plus virtual-time, sequence-lifetime and concurrent-shutdown clauses.

Diagnostic sequence-affinity checks (RFC 0001 rank 11; R10-SEQCHECK): SequenceChecker stays valid across the threads of one sequence over a 4-thread pool, rejects another sequence, a plain thread and off-runner calls, binds to threads outside tasks and to single-thread runners' threads, treats a manual runner's tasks as its sequence, and rebinds after Detach; a thread-only checker must fail the cross-thread clause, and PLATFORM_CHECK_SEQUENCE must abort a child process that breaks the rule.

The shared task-runner suite must catch seven broken providers on the clause each breaks (LIFO sequence, overlapping sequence, delays ignored, accepts after shutdown, runs after shutdown, runs inline, claims every thread) while a conforming control passes.

platform.record-store.v1 (player records such as gamestate.txt): the shared suite (invalid keys, not found vs failure, exact round trip of every byte and of an empty record, whole replacement, independent keys, an exact size limit whose refusal keeps the record, a restart sees the last commits, concurrent commits and loads never tear) against the in-memory fake and the file store (platform/records), plus the file store's clauses: <directory>/<key> keeps gamestate.txt where the file system wrote it, a leftover staging file changes nothing, a missing directory fails cleanly, an oversized file is refused.

The platform.record-store.v1 suite rejects ten broken stores (accepts invalid keys, reports a missing record as a failure, treats an empty record as missing, stops at a NUL byte, appends, clobbers on an oversized commit, ignores its limit, truncates keys, publishes torn records, forgets on restart) while the conforming fake passes.

The shared platform.record-store.v1 suite against the user-defaults store (platform/apple; the tvOS product's gamestate.txt store) in the device's real standard user defaults, plus its layout (NSData under source.records.<key>) and foreign-value clauses. Runs on iOS and tvOS devices through tools/quality/ios_conformance.py; unavailable on hosts.

platform.achievement-service.v1 (Game Center on iOS/tvOS): the shared suite (invalid IDs, signed-out reports wait and are delivered once at sign-in, accepted IDs are not resubmitted, refused deliveries retry at the next report or sign-in, in-flight IDs are not resubmitted, late completions after the service is gone are harmless, the achievements screen and completion banner follow sign-in and the platform, concurrent reports each delivered once with the platform completing inside Submit) against QueuedAchievementService over a scripted platform.

The platform.achievement-service.v1 suite rejects nine broken services (accepts invalid IDs, submits while signed out, drops reports made while signed out, never retries, resubmits accepted or in-flight IDs, shows the screen or claims the banner while signed out, ignores the platform's banner) while the defect-free build of the same service passes.

The Game Center bridge (platform/apple) under QueuedAchievementService on a real device: authentication resolves with GKLocalPlayer's state, Submit completes exactly once and never accepts while signed out, the signed-out service shows no screen and claims no banner, the bridge claims Game Center's banner. The conformance app has no Game Center entitlement, so it covers the signed-out path. Runs through tools/quality/ios_conformance.py; unavailable on hosts.

render.presentation.v1 "Dynamic range" on the SDL3-Vulkan pair on an iPhone or Apple TV (MoltenVK). An extended-linear kRGBA16Float presentation gets a half-float swapchain in extended linear sRGB, keeps 4.0 (four times SDR white) in the presented image, sets the Metal layer to high dynamic range, and sees the screen's current headroom rise above 1 while it presents. A standard presentation on the same window is the control: it clips 4.0 to white, reports headroom 1 and returns the layer to standard. The frames alternate SDR white and brighter-than-white. Runs through tools/quality/ios_conformance.py; unavailable on hosts.

render.output.v1 on a display (RFC 0016 K11): render_lab's presenting host (render/lab/app) shows its HDR chart (a gray ramp from 1/64 to 16 times SDR white, gray and warm patches from 0.18 to 16, saturated patches at 4) on an iPhone or Apple TV through render.pass.output and the SDL3-Vulkan bridge (MoltenVK), with the back buffer imported into the core as a port texture. The extended-linear range is granted and the Metal layer shows high range; the headroom rises above 1; on tvOS the window asks for the HDR mode and the TV switches into it (headroom at least 1.5, needs Match Dynamic Range on). Every patch of the presented swapchain image equals the output oracle's tone map at the frame's headroom within 0.4 percent, values above white reach the display, and a debug view presents the 16x patch untouched. Control: a standard 8-bit presentation at the legacy point shows the clip and sRGB within one level, and on tvOS withdraws the HDR request. RENDER_LAB_SHOW_SECONDS keeps the chart on screen afterwards. Runs through tools/quality/ios_conformance.py --app render_lab; unavailable on hosts.

RFC 0016 K4 'Artifacts per target' (tools/render/shader_artifacts.py check). Every shader module the native backend ships (the regenerators' material table, every shaders/legacy stage and the demo_triangle_spv.h arrays: 204 units) is built into one artifact per target format: SPIR-V with the pinned glslc and GLSL 4.50 with the pinned SPIRV-Cross (cross_compiler in quality/toolchain/shader-compiler.json) after flattening bind groups into GL slot ranges of 16, each GLSL artifact compiling as OpenGL GLSL with the pinned glslangValidator. Artifacts are keyed by source, compiler identity, format and permutation (the options that vary between a source's units, one bit each), and unique. Each SPIR-V artifact's reflection (spirv-cross --reflect) must match its declared pass or family in render/shaders/layouts.json (set, binding, kind, count, stage, push-constant stage), every declaration must be used, every unit must have exactly one owner, and a family may declare at most four groups in role order. The build's generated headers (every shader_toolchain.GENERATED_NAMES header, none committed since RFC 0016 K4) must all be written, material_spv.h, material_spv_index.h and legacy_spv.h must agree with the regenerators' independent --check --compare-dir writers, and each demo_triangle_spv.h array must equal its artifact. Declared GLSL 4.50 exclusions (ray query; the two seven-set passes) must still fail to cross-compile. About 3 s on 32 threads.

Test chamber signs light up and cast their light at runtime, on native Vulkan's legacy world path (tools/quality/portal_sign_light.py suite --path legacy; RFC 0011 emissive area lights, light set v2).
